scenario.name: NIST SP 800-86 & Microsoft DFIR — Event Log Clearing via wevtutil.exe & USN Journal Recovery (EID 1102 / 104)
scenario.overview: Imagine a burglar who breaks into a bank security booth right before leaving and rips out every single page from every logbook on the shelf. Unbeknownst to the burglar, the moment the security logbook is ripped empty, an automatic brass stamper permanently embosses a fresh Page One declaring exactly who emptied the book and at what second, while the building master floor-tile register still keeps carbon impressions of every ripped page underneath. In this scenario (T1070.001, NIST SP 800-86 & Microsoft DFIR, Event Log Clearing via wevtutil.exe & USN Journal Recovery , EID 1102 / 104), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mass Channel Enumeration, then immutable Audit Log Cleared Events, then nTFS $UsnJrnl:$J Transaction Correlation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Mass Channel Enumeration, then Immutable Audit Log Cleared Events, then NTFS $UsnJrnl:$J Transaction Correlation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Mass Channel Enumeration & wevtutil.exe cl Execution (Sysmon EventID 1)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1070.001 - Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs)
stages.description: Trying to cover their tracks right before slipping out the door, the intruder runs an automated sweeper that lists every single diary binder on the building shelf and commands the event clerk to wipe them clean one by one. To erase post-exploitation traces before disconnecting, the attacker runs cmd.exe /c "for /F %i in ('wevtutil.exe el') do wevtutil.exe cl "%i"" or PowerShell Clear-EventLog. Real-time SIEM forwarding captures the Sysmon EventID 1 / Security EventID 4688 process creation before the local .evtx files on disk are truncated (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, Image=C:\Windows\System32\wevtutil.exe, CommandLine=wevtutil.exe cl Security, ApiInvoked=wevtapi.dll!EvtClearLog so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes for /F "tokens=*" %1 in ('wevtutil.exe el') do wevtutil.exe cl "%1" (which invokes the Windows Event Collector CLI utility , wevtutil.exe with the cl , clear-log or el , enum-logs parameter to instruct svchost.exe , EventL so that attempts anti-forensic indicator removal , T1070.001 during "Mass Channel Enumeration & wevtutil.exe cl Execution , Sysmon EventID 1" by wiping recorded Windows Security, System, PowerShell, or Sysmon audit trails, which immediately causes the OS to write Security EventID 1102 or System EventID 104 and USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION in $UsnJrnl:$J). Next, the follow-up artifact powershell.exe -Command "Get-WinEvent -ListLog * | ForEach-Object { [System.Diagnostics.Eventing.Reader.EventLogSession]::GlobalSession.ClearLog($_.LogName) }" runs (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1070.001 during "Mass Channel Enumeration & wevtutil.exe cl Execution , Sysmon EventID 1" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ wevtutil.exe cl Security / ⇠#1 ACK 1) from Node ① (#1 Attacker Cleanup Script) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 NTFS $UsnJrnl:$J & EVTX Slack).

Under the hood, the observed step executes MFTECmd.exe -f "C:\$Extend\$UsnJrnl:$J" --csv C:\Forensics # Shows USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION on Security.evtx (which Parses or manipulates low-level NTFS Master File Table , $MFT record attributes, comparing the user-modifiable $STANDARD_INFORMATION , 0x10 timesta so that exposes anti-forensic timestomping , NtSetInformationFile · T1070.001 or deleted file activity during "NTFS $UsnJrnl:$J Transaction Correlation & Unallocated EVTX Chunk Carving , ElfChnk" by proving that the 0x10 creation timestamp was backdated earlier than the immutable 0x30 kernel creation timestamp). Next, the follow-up artifact EVTX 64KB Chunk Header Magic: 45 6C 66 43 68 6E 6B 00 ("ElfChnk\x00") runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , EVTX 64KB Chunk Header Magic: 45 6C 66 43 68 6E 6B 00 , "ElfChnk\x00" via System / Runtime E so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1070.001 during "NTFS $UsnJrnl:$J Transaction Correlation & Unallocated EVTX Chunk Carving , ElfChnk" , During disk forensics, the analyst parses the NTFS Change Journal , $Extend\$UsnJrnl:$J showing USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION , 0x00000200 on Security while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ MFTECmd.exe -f C:\$Extend\$UsnJrnl:$J (USN_REASON_DATA_TRUNCATION on Security.evtx) / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 EventLog RPC (EvtClearLog)) to Node ④ (#4 svchost.exe (EventLog Service)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 NTFS $UsnJrnl:$J & EVTX Slack).
